rationale: Both replace the character scanner with a line-based pass and include good refactoring notes. A stays simple: one loop with an inList flag, a small isListItem predicate, and a headerLevel helper. Its emphasize helper wraps an actual pair of markers rather than blindly replacing the first two occurrences. B introduces a renderer struct with four state flags and five open/close methods to manage elements that, for single-line headers and items, could simply be closed on the same line. That reintroduces some of the stateful complexity the refactor was meant to remove. B also treats any line starting with '*' as a list item, and silently merges consecutive paragraph lines. A is clearer and has less needless machinery.
